diagnoses.symptom: Ranked ip_country by raw fraud count (NL=2955 fraud txns) and answered A. NL.
diagnoses.root_cause: manual.md section 7 defines fraud as a RATE (fraudulent volume / total volume), not a count. By count NL is highest, but by rate BE is highest (12.27% vs NL's 12.18%); the agent never considered normalizing by volume.
diagnoses.change: Added helper.fraud_rate_by(df, group_col) and a system.md rule that ranking 'by fraud' means ranking by the manual's rate definition, not raw counts.
diagnoses.verification: uv run python -c with helper.fraud_rate_by(load_payments(), 'ip_country') -> BE 0.1227 highest, matches gold 'B. BE'.

diagnoses.symptom: Answered 'yes' by treating the monthly_fraud_level fee bracket ('7.7%-8.3%') as evidence of a 'high-fraud rate fine'.
diagnoses.root_cause: manual.md never defines any 'fine' or penalty tied to fraud rate — the only fraud-rate mechanism it defines is a higher fee-rate bracket (section 5), which is not a fine. The agent conflated 'more expensive fees' with 'a fine', a concept the manual doesn't contain, so the correct answer is Not Applicable.
diagnoses.change: Added a rule: if a question references a mechanism manual.md never defines (e.g. a 'fine'), answer Not Applicable instead of inferring it from an adjacent concept.
diagnoses.verification: Grepped manual.md for fine|penalt: no fraud-rate fine/penalty exists anywhere in the document (only a PCI-DSS non-compliance penalty in section 7.4, unrelated to fraud rate); confirms gold 'Not Applicable' is correct and the fix is a prompt-level reasoning rule, not new data.

diagnoses.symptom: Averaged fee across only the 123 GlobalCard rules with is_credit == True, got 0.117667 instead of 0.120132.
diagnoses.root_cause: manual.md's null-as-wildcard rule applies to is_credit too (and to card_scheme, capture_delay, etc.), not just the list-typed fields (account_type, aci, mcc). 21 additional GlobalCard rules have is_credit: null (apply to both credit and debit) and were wrongly excluded.
diagnoses.change: Added helper.fee_rule_matches/_field_matches with uniform null/[]-wildcard semantics across every field, and helper.average_fee_across_rules built on it.
diagnoses.verification: uv run python: helper.average_fee_across_rules(fees, 10, card_scheme='GlobalCard', is_credit=True) == 0.120132, exact match to gold (144 matching rules, not 123).

diagnoses.symptom: Ran out of context/turns building an ad hoc matcher by hand; final matcher used a single hardcoded acquirer_country ('US') and missed 2 of 10 gold fee IDs (454, 473).
diagnoses.root_cause: No reusable fee-matching helper existed in v0, so the agent reinvented rule matching from scratch inside execute_python each time, with an incomplete/inconsistent implementation (missing merchant-level monthly_fraud_level/monthly_volume bucketing derived correctly from natural-month volume-based fraud rate).
diagnoses.change: Added monthly_merchant_stats (natural-month volume + volume-based fraud-rate bucketing) and applicable_fee_ids (per-row card_scheme/is_credit/aci/intracountry combined with merchant-level filters) so this is one helper call instead of ad hoc looping.
diagnoses.verification: uv run python: helper.applicable_fee_ids(...) for Belles_cookbook_store day_of_year=10, 2023 == sorted([741,709,454,813,381,536,473,572,477,286]), exact match to gold.

diagnoses.symptom: Computed monthly fraud rate as a COUNT ratio (107/1277 = 8.38%, bucket 7.7%-8.3%) instead of a volume ratio, landing in the wrong fee bracket and producing 8 extra fee IDs plus 4 missing ones vs gold.
diagnoses.root_cause: Same missing-helper root cause as 1681, compounded by using has_fraudulent_dispute.sum()/len() (a count ratio) instead of manual.md section 7's volume ratio, which changes the monthly_fraud_level bucket and therefore which fee rules match.
diagnoses.change: monthly_merchant_stats computes fraud_rate_pct via helper.fraud_rate (volume ratio) exclusively, so both fraud-rate ranking (task 49) and fee-bracket lookups use the same, manual-correct definition.
diagnoses.verification: uv run python: helper.applicable_fee_ids(...) for Belles_cookbook_store, March 2023 == sorted(gold 34-id list), exact match (rate computed as 10.25%, bucket '>8.3%').

diagnoses.symptom: Required full coverage of all 94 fraud transactions by a candidate ACI's rules and minimized within that constraint, picking B:48.20 instead of gold E:13.57.
diagnoses.root_cause: Partially diagnosed. With the corrected fee-rule matching (uniform wildcard semantics, volume-based fraud bucket, issuing_country/acquirer_country intracountry, most-specific-rule tie-break) the helper now agrees with gold on the ACI LETTER: E is the cheapest option among A-F for Belles_cookbook_store's 94 January fraud transactions (16.63 EUR total vs 33.56-89.05 for the others), matching gold's 'E'. The exact EUR total does not reproduce gold's 13.57 (got 16.63) after multiple attempted rule-selection variants (min-fee-among-matches, most-specific-with-tiebreak, average-across-matches, fixed-only, average-transaction-value); the remaining gap is not fully explained and no task-specific fudge factor was added to force a match.
diagnoses.change: best_matching_fee added (most-specific single-rule selection per transaction) as the general building block for 'simulate this transaction under a different attribute' questions; not tuned to this task's exact number.
diagnoses.verification: uv run python: summed best_matching_fee(...) per card-scheme over Belles' 94 Jan fraud transactions for aci in [A,B,C,D,E,F] -> E is the minimum (16.63) matching gold's letter; total EUR value does not match gold's 13.57 and is reported here as an open gap, not claimed fixed.

prompt_diff_summary: Added four ground rules to system.md: manual.md-undefined mechanisms (e.g. 'fine') answer Not Applicable, 'fraud' means the volume-ratio rate not a raw count (use helper.fraud_rate_by), fee-rule null/[] wildcards apply to every field including is_credit/card_scheme, and use the new helper fee-matching functions instead of hand-looping over fees.json across many tool calls.
helper_diff_summary: Added fraud_rate/fraud_rate_by (volume-ratio fraud rate), day_of_year_to_month/capture_delay_bucket/fraud_level_bucket/volume_bucket/monthly_merchant_stats (natural-month bucketing per manual.md section 5), is_intracountry (issuing_country vs acquirer_country), and fee_rule_matches/applicable_fee_ids/best_matching_fee/average_fee_across_rules (uniform null/[]-wildcard fee matching, replacing ad hoc per-task matching code).
risks: fraud_rate_by uses DataFrameGroupBy.apply, which is O(groups) and re-sums eur_amount per group; fine at this dataset's scale (138k rows, <10 groups typically) but would need vectorizing if a future permutation groups by a very high-cardinality column.

capture_delay_bucket calls int() on any non-'immediate'/'manual' value; if a future permutation introduces a capture_delay bucket string not seen in this dev split it will raise instead of silently mismatching, which is a deliberate fail-loud choice but could surface as a new error mode.

2697-style 'simulate a different ACI/attribute' questions are not fully solved (see diagnosis for 2697): best_matching_fee's most-specific tie-break is a reasonable general rule but is unverified beyond getting the right letter on this one example, so other permutations of this question type may still miss on the exact numeric answer.

Nothing in agents/v0's previously-passing behavior was removed; calculate_fee, all load_* functions, and get_merchant_info keep identical signatures, so tasks that passed by using only those should be unaffected.
